verdict.rationale: The IRS maintains versioned, per-tax-year XML schema packages, business rules, and SOAP A2A WSDLs for its Modernized e-File machine channel, so a machine-readable specification does exist. Distribution is gated: schemas come only through the registered-user portal or e-Services mailbox, the WSDL toolkit is sent on email request, and no OpenAPI spec is published (all candidate paths return 404). missing for 10: public, unauthenticated download of the XML schemas/WSDLs, a public OpenAPI or data-dictionary artifact, a public version/deprecation policy, and a published schema for the IRIS A2A channel.

support.subject: As a developer, a machine-readable specification for the service's machine channel is published — an OpenAPI spec, XML schemas, or a data dictionary

citations.quote: Schemas and business rules are now available through the registered user portal and your e-services mailbox
Federal returns must conform to valid schema versions.
MeF uses the widely accepted Extensible Markup Language (XML) format.
